newsitem.title: UK: Last three November Brents deferred to Dec - trade.
newsitem.headline: Last three November Brents deferred to Dec - trade.

text.p: The last three Brent cargoes due to be nominated loading dates in November have been deferred and will now load in December, trade sources said on Wednesday.
The three cargoes were originally due to load November 25-27 and November 28-30, they said.
The cargoes will be included in the December loading programme due to be released on Thursday or Friday, traders said.
Traders said the equity holders, British Petroleum and Exxon, were aiming to maximise the value of the cargoes by moving them from a weak November spot market into December.
"If they load in November they achieve a lower realised value than they can get by putting them in December," said a Brent market player.
"The November/December (paper) spread is negative so December is worth more to them," he added.
The spot Brent market has seen active trade this week at discounts of between 40 and 50 cents to December forward paper values.

On Monday one full cargo was added to the November loading programme, taking it to 39 standard 500,000-barrel cargoes plus 2.17 million barrels in top-ups, but Wednesday's deferrals trim November's tally to 36 full cargoes.
"These three will be added to the December programme," said an equity holder.
